engines.name: Interfaze 1.1 Lite (MoA dev workloads, OpenAI-compatible)
engines.hardware: hosted (api.interfaze.ai); self-host needs an 80 GB GPU

status.status: released; not yet measured by JevBench

engines.notes: Mixture-of-agents model for dev workloads (document OCR, speech, grounding, structured output). `nur jev start --engine interfaze-1-lite` bridges System One onto its OpenAI chat endpoint with JSON-schema probabilities; INTERFAZE_API_KEY is read from the environment, or `nur jev login interfaze-1-lite` stores one. Self-host: the repository's Docker image serves /v1 on port 8000, and a loopback --upstream needs no key.

engines.name: Liquid d1 (Liquid AI Console, hosted System One)

status.status: released; not yet measured by JevBench

engines.notes: The paid d1 tier on Liquid's own endpoint (up to 8 images per request, 4.5 MB body). The same model through OpenRouter Decisions is the `liquid-d1` entry. Keys come from console.liquid.ai (liquid_...). Store one with `nur jev login liquid-d1-ultra` or export LIQUID_AI_API_KEY; the liquid-d1-ultra, liquid-d1-direct and liquid-d1-free engines share that one slot. nur reads LIQUID_AI_API_KEY rather than the LIQUID_API_KEY Liquid's docs name, because LIQUID_API_KEY already belongs to the Liquid Inference chat route.
